verdicts.reason: A: the CTA, a tiny jar thumbnail, the logo and the 'CLINICALLY TESTED' eyebrow are jammed into one cramped bottom row, so the eyebrow ends up last in the reading order. The leaf image is cut down to a thin strip, and the dense legal block is so large it competes with the headline on the right. B: the headline and CTA hierarchy reads better, but the Lumen & Fig logo and jar shrink to near-invisible specks crushed against a tiny, low-contrast, unreadable legal block. The eyebrow sits below the subhead, the leaves are pushed into a sliver at the far edge, and a dead gap sits in the middle, so B loses more of the brand.
